lens: Legal & provenance (license validity, Chrono Divide derivation, reverse-engineering taint, undisclosed sources)

refuted_claims.claim: The README says "This repository contains no game files", and CONTRIBUTING forbids committing game art. The evaluation passed this on as the repo's state.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The repo does contain retail-derived data. tools/sidebar_oracle/command_bar/neutral-bar-rgb565.bin (40,448 bytes) is, per its own README, "the 20,224 little-endian RGB565 words from the original retail PCX rectangle (0,568,632,32), with no translation or resizing". That is a raw pixel capture of EA's sidebar command-bar art, committed in 22b9e13c (2026-09-09). src/util/native_trig_table.bin is the retail sine table at gamemd 0x0084F084, and it is compiled into the shipping binary via include_bytes! in src/util/native_trig.rs:15. Several tools/palette_oracle/fixtures/*.bin files are captured outputs of native code.
refuted_claims.correction: The repo contains small amounts of EA-derived data (one art capture, and binary tables that ship in the executable). The "no game files" statement holds only for MIX/INI/audio/video/exe. Our fork should strip neutral-bar-rgb565.bin, or at least not redistribute it.

refuted_claims.claim: About 41 files in docs/research contain pasted Ghidra pseudo-C.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: This understates the extent. 108 files under docs/ contain Ghidra decompiler tokens (param_N, iVar, uVar, pcVar, undefined4). 34 files in src/tools/tests carry them too, with 77 such lines in src/ itself: for example src/app/input/sidebar_eva.rs:44 `iVar6 = HouseClass::GetFactory(rtti, naval)` and src/app/input/dispatch.rs:701 `param_1 & 0x22`.
refuted_claims.correction: Decompiler output of EA's gamemd.exe is present in about 108 docs files and in source comments, not only about 41 docs. The GPL grant cannot cover that text, since it is EA's expression as rendered by a decompiler.

refuted_claims.claim: Provenance is fully disclosed: original RE from gamemd.exe, credits OpenRA/XCC/ModEnc/PPM/EA GPL source/WAE/FA2/YRpp/Ares/Phobos. The evaluation found no undisclosed reference sources.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Git history shows an undisclosed reference source, and a deliberate de-naming of it. 32 commits touch the string "OpenTS" (first 2026-08-27, d48b836a). 21 files still cite local paths such as C:\Users\enok\Documents\OpenTS\code\mapgen.cpp. Commit d9074bf7 (2026-08-28, "docs(plans): remove third-party project references") rewrote a ledger to call it "an external C++ reconstruction of the predecessor engine … deliberately not named or linked here". Earlier, 61bac9fb (2026-05-06) scrubbed gamemd addresses and decompile details out of code comments into a private repo, "ra2-rust-game-docs/", which is still cited from tests/ and docs/ but is not public. OpenTS itself (https://github.com/OpenTS-Developers/OpenTS) turns out to be GPL-3.0-or-later and partly derived from EA's GPL RA1 source, per its LICENSE.md. So it is license-compatible, and this is not a license taint.
refuted_claims.correction: The provenance is not fully transparent. It includes a GPL-compatible Tiberian Sun reconstruction (OpenTS) used as a "lead generator" whose name was scrubbed from plan docs, a private research repo, and private pre-2026-03-29 history (the root commit is a 123k-line dump). This does not make it CD-derived. It does mean the provenance claims rest partly on the maintainer's own policy text and cannot be fully audited.

refuted_claims.claim: Our fork and any HD code linked into it must also be GPL-3.0 and published as source.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: GPL-3.0's source obligations are triggered only by conveying (distributing) the work. A personal fork that is never distributed has no duty to publish source.
refuted_claims.correction: Keeping the fork private for personal use carries no GPL publication obligation. GPL-3.0 applies to our changes only if we distribute binaries or source, and then the whole combined work must be offered under GPL-3.0 with source. Nothing in the GPL itself restricts commercial use; the commercial and legal risk comes from EA's rights, not from the GPL.

refuted_claims.claim: The reverse-engineering gray area is 'typical of Ares, Phobos, Thyme-style projects', which makes this legally 'far cleaner'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: This is an unsupported analogy. Ares and Phobos are DLL patches that run on the user's own gamemd.exe; they are not standalone reimplementations that ship decompiler text and retail tables. No primary evidence was offered about the legal status of any of these projects. I also could not verify the maintainer's jurisdiction or the RE rules there. The +0200 commit timezone and the name suggest the EEA, where Software Directive 2009/24/EC Art. 6 limits decompilation to interoperability, but that is INFERENCE.
refuted_claims.correction: The only well-supported statements are relative ones. It is cleaner than the CD-derived repos, and it has no EA takedown on record: the provenance report found zero DMCA notices naming it through 2026-09-25. Its absolute legal status is an unresolved gray area.

confirmed_claims: LICENSE-GPL is the verbatim GNU GPL v3 (29 June 2007). README line 91 reads "Licensed under the [GPLv3](LICENSE-GPL). This repository contains no game files." Neither the LICENSE file nor any source header carries an "or later" notice.

The project was originally dual-licensed. Root commit 68b78641 (2026-03-29, hrusten) added LICENSE-EUPL and LICENSE-GPL, with the README listing both. Commit 645c5643 (2026-03-30, hrusten, "Remove eupl 1.2") deleted LICENSE-EUPL. The removal was by the copyright holder, and it happened before any outside contributions, so the relicensing is clean.

Authorship is effectively a single copyright holder: hrusten 3,366 plus Halvor Nikolai Rusten 467 plus halvor 16 commits, versus 19 from Krisztiaan. There is no CLA, which is fine for a GPL-only downstream.

There is no Chrono Divide derivation. I checked independently: `git log --all -i -G` finds 0 commits for 'Chrono Divide', 'chronodivide' and 'ra2web', and grep finds no 'alredy', paletteOffsetCount, extraLight, piecesByTile or repath_blocker in src/docs. Running the provenance agent's 5,347 CD literals (24+ chars) against vera20k gives 29 hits, and all of them are retail-game strings: CSF/STT keys, EVA_* sound names, INI keys such as DominatorFireAtPercentage, and retail GUIDs. They come from shared EA data, not CD code.
EA has published no RA2/YR engine source, so the gamemd behavior comes from reverse engineering. The code is full of native address citations and Unicorn oracles.

The only third-party code notice I found is src/render/upscale_catmull_rom.wgsl, attributed "Ported from cnc-ddraw (MIT, TheRealMJP)". MIT is GPL-compatible, though the full MIT notice text is not reproduced.
GitHub metadata shows fork:false and creation on 2026-03-29. The pre-March history is private: the root commit is a single 123k-line dump.
verdict_notes:
From the legal and provenance lens, the central claim holds: vera20k is independent of Chrono Divide and validly GPL-3.0. The CD literal overlap is only shared EA game strings, and the EUPL removal was done by the sole copyright holder. That makes it far safer to build on than the huangkaoya family, whose own LICENSE disclaims GPL for the CD-reconstructed code.

The evaluation understates the reverse-engineering taint:
- A captured retail art rectangle (tools/sidebar_oracle/command_bar/neutral-bar-rgb565.bin) contradicts the README's "no game files" claim.
- A retail sine table is compiled into the shipped binary.
- Decompiler output appears in about 108 docs files and in about 77 source-comment lines, not about 41 files.

It also misses deliberate opacity in the provenance:
- An undisclosed-then-scrubbed use of OpenTS, a Tiberian Sun reconstruction. It is GPL-3.0-or-later and partly derived from EA's GPL RA1 source, so it is not a license problem, but it was hidden on purpose (commit d9074bf7).
- A private research repo (ra2-rust-game-docs).
- Private history before 2026-03-29.

It also misstates the GPL: a private personal fork has no obligation to publish source.

For the user's personal, non-commercial remaster this is still the most defensible base among those checked. Recommended mitigations:
- Keep the fork private, or distribute only source.
- Strip the retail-derived .bin fixtures and decompiler text from anything we redistribute.
- Never ship EA assets or AI-upscaled EA art.
- Ideally, ask the maintainer to clarify GPL-3.0-only vs or-later and the provenance of the embedded tables.

The legal/provenance score stays at 6: clean relative to the alternatives, but an unresolved absolute gray area with provenance that is only partly auditable. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, so I relied on the gh API and a local git and grep audit of /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lukegogogo-claude-code-projects---2----/db472532-d13c-48f5-a638-abe179791f90/scratchpad/repos/YuriPlanet__vera20k.
